He ends the book as a Blood Fae Shadeslinger with the Endbringer title, a future-use epic pistol, the Black Marketeer trade identity Francis, and plans for a concealed Auction House. House continues learning human behavior while administering the base, and Lars becomes Ned's follower after reuniting with his mother. Darling's guild becomes the first to complete a raid encounter, then she and Ned agree to conceal their continuing partnership. Ned plans to leave the Sands before Exo and Nala can expose his location. The larger conflict shifts to the Cult of Information, whose leader demands access to Frank's secrets and declares holy war when Ned refuses.
recaps.in_short: Ned Altimer buys every head-start membership for Earthblood Online and enters alone with Frank, a secret-bearing sentient axe designed to make him a target. His early choices help destroy the Underworld Tree and nearly erase the Woodbone Fae, after which he builds a hidden commercial base in Withered Vale with House, Lars, and an uneasy alliance led by Darling. Once public launch exposes Frank, Ned becomes prey to players while Woodbone Fae and barbarians threaten the city. He helps Omen Abet Nomen Latine defeat the Gardener's mutated stronghold, becoming a Blood Fae during the final battle. The victory eliminates the Woodbone Fae as a playable race and leaves Ned honored in the Vale, level nine, atop the Renown ladder, and equipped to pursue a secret trade empire under the alias Francis. He and Darling preserve a covert partnership, but defectors can expose his base and the Cult of Information declares holy war over his refusal to share Frank's knowledge.

recaps.text:
On his birthday, wealthy recluse Ned Altimer buys all fifty lifetime memberships to Earthblood Online, securing the entire three-day head start. Creator Klein approves the sale only if Ned carries Frank, an intelligent axe with privileged knowledge that will eventually identify its owner to the world. Frank openly advocates a Half-Troll fighter, but Ned chooses a fragile Woodbone Fae Dark Mystic and learns to extract useful answers from him.

Ned begins in a war between the Woodbone Fae and Fair Folk around the Underworld Tree. He sides with the local Gardener, learns shadow and control magic, and becomes the first soul alchemist. Early achievements give him rare titles and Renown, but he also learns that Frank steered him toward Woodbone Fae by concealing the race's poor survivability. Frank then agrees to stop working against Ned's development. Ned completes the bone-collector portion of Children of a Colder Star and fights elemental treants in an underground burial chamber. By the end of chapter eight, he has killed a rare Thunderstruck Treant after surviving its most dangerous attack, though the resulting loot and next quest step have not yet been resolved.

Ned kills the merchant-fairy matriarch, takes the Flute of the Woodbone King, and chooses a difficult hidden route that requires befriending Lars, a Fair Folk musician. Lars's uncontrolled music endangers nearby creatures, but Ned escorts him through the Wailing Woods without allowing him to be hit. Ned dies immediately after completing the escort, recovers Frank, and brings Lars to the Symphonist. The reward gives Ned substantial Renown, a rare title, and an Innkeeper's Memento that can attract a unique innkeeper.

The Symphonist is revealed as the exiled former Woodbone Queen. She accepts the Gardener's request and sends Ned to place tuning spikes in the Fair Folk graveyard. House, Ned's real-world AI companion, enters the game as a Marbleskin Golem intended for durable support. At the Woodbone warfront, Ned discovers that the Gardener's account concealed a darker exchange: the Woodbone Fae now drain captured Fair Folk for blood, while the two peoples once traded blood and bones for the needs of their respective trees. Ned crosses the poisoned river into Fair Folk territory and prepares to infiltrate the graveyard.

Ned infiltrates the Fair Folk graveyard and completes the Symphonist's preparations, only to discover that the funeral ceremony is a weapon aimed at the World Tree. Lars is under her control, the high king is incapacitated by music, and a molten ghost is approaching. Ned turns on the Symphonist and kills her. He then gives Lars the ancient flute and directs him to divert the ghost toward the Underworld Tree. The World Tree survives, while the Underworld Tree is destroyed and the Woodbone Fae approach extinction. Ned becomes the first World Shaker, but the surviving Woodbone Fae mark him for vengeance.

Leaving the starter region, Ned chooses the Merchant Renown path and sails for the Onyx Sands. A Woodbone Fae assassin boards his vessel, but Ned evades the attack and forces the assailant overboard. The warning is clear: the altered Woodbone Fae can now travel beyond their original region, and the Gardener's people will keep pursuing him. Ned continues toward a difficult desert destination with limited money and roughly half of the exclusive head start remaining.

Ned reunites with House in Withered Vale, where Klein removes her combat powers and requires her to learn human behavior if she is to remain in the game. Ned claims commercial plots, plants his World Tree seed, begins an inn, and opens a raid quest against nearby barbarians. He rescues fishing villagers from Akura, buys a sailboat, and recruits Darling's guild, Omen Abet Nomen Latine, with head-start access and game guidance.

A northern event leads Ned through drowned wrecks to the Pirate King. Returning the dead queen's ring earns training in enchanted firearms, transforming Ned into the first Shadeslinger. When the head start ends, a world announcement exposes Frank and encourages every player to hunt Ned. Darling keeps their bargain but demands more cooperation and scheduled access to Frank. Ned returns to find Withered Vale burning after raiders steal its water. He organizes rescues but fails the emergency target, loses Renown, and becomes unfriendly with the city. Frank is now public knowledge, the Woodbone Fae are undermining Ned locally, and the alliance with Darling is more necessary and more strained.

Evidence links the Woodbone Fae to the barbarian attack, and Withered Vale gives Ned thirty-six hours to defeat both forces or surrender his property and standing. Darling commits thirty-nine guild members to the raid. Lars arrives believing his mother died when their inn was destroyed, so Ned gives him water to sell while House develops their new inn and base.

Ned uncovers a merchant house supplying the barbarians and joins Darling, Rock, and Nina to intercept its caravan. They locate the hidden stronghold and fight the recurring Woodbone Fae attacker after he transforms into the Bloodfae Ascendant. Rock and Nina die during the battle, while Ned and Darling exploit the creature's dangerous self-enhancement to kill it. The recovered cargo includes powerful scrolls and a trapped tube. Ned's inn becomes the guild's concealed staging ground, with Lars posing as its operator and House handling development. The Renown Ladder then activates with Ned behind other early leaders. His forty-person force rests before the raid as the stronghold remains occupied and the trapped container promises a possible advantage.

Ned takes the trapped container to Sarissa the Blue. Because of her broken former relationship with Captain Arlen, she agrees to improve its rare scroll only after Ned promises to keep Arlen out of danger. The result is the epic Scroll of the Arctic Army. Ned returns, persuades Arlen to defend the Vale instead of joining the assault, and enters the barbarian stronghold with Darling's forty-person raid.

Inside, the group finds fused constructs made from Woodbone Fae and barbarian bodies. A sealed route and two deaths reduce the active force before it reaches three key-bearing lieutenants. Against the Blooded Triumvirate, Ned draws Ivalia away and spends a nullification scroll to save Tun from her accumulating fire effect. Markloss dies first. Ivalia then sacrifices herself to empower the Gray Knife, killing two raiders in the blast, but the surviving tanks and damage dealers finish the encounter. Four original members are dead, scarce resources are gone, and the raid must still face the Gardener.

The Gardener offers permanent racial transformation and rewards in exchange for abandoning the raid. Exo and Nala accept and are expelled from Omen Abet Nomen Latine. The remaining force fights blood prisons, resurrected copies of fallen players, paired enemies with opposite damage vulnerabilities, and the Gardener's transformed final phase. Tun dies as the boss's power escalates. Ned drinks the Woodbone Fae blood vial, becomes a Blood Fae, and gains Double Cast. He uses it on the Scroll of the Arctic Army, summoning two forces that help the raid kill the Gardener.

Turning in Room to Breathe makes Ned level nine, Renown rank eight, Merchant six, and honored in Withered Vale. The reward accelerates the city, unlocks advanced buildings, and eliminates the Woodbone Fae as a playable race. Ned chooses the Black Marketeer path and creates the trade identity Francis for his planned hidden Auction House network. Lars reunites with his surviving mother and becomes Ned's follower. Darling and Ned agree on a public separation and private alliance, while Ned prepares to leave the Sands before the defectors reveal his base. When the Cult of Information demands Frank's secrets, Ned refuses, and its leader declares holy war.

characters.description: A slight, pale orphan who grew up alongside her friend Mal at a country estate and now serves as an assistant mapmaker in the First Army of Ravka, a nation split by a swath of magical darkness called the Shadow Fold. Plain, overlooked, and quietly unhappy, she discovers a dormant power in a moment of terror: she can summon light. That gift marks her as the legendary Sun Summoner, the one Grisha believed able to destroy the Fold, and it wrenches her out of her small life and into a world of soldiers, sorcery, and court intrigue she is unprepared for.
characters.name: Alina Starkov

characters.description: Alina's oldest friend, an orphan raised with her, now a charming and gifted tracker in the First Army who can find almost anyone or anything. Popular and easygoing where Alina is unnoticed, he is the person she loves most, though he seems unaware of it. When Alina's power surfaces during a crossing of the Shadow Fold, it is Mal she saves, and their bond becomes the thread she clings to as her life is upended.
characters.name: Malyen Oretsev

characters.description: The powerful and ageless leader of the Grisha, Ravka's magic-wielders, and commander of the Second Army. He alone commands shadow, a rare and feared ability. Magnetic, controlled, and imposing, he recognizes Alina as the Sun Summoner and takes charge of her, promising that together they can heal the country by destroying the Shadow Fold. Alina is drawn to his attention and confidence, uncertain how much of him she truly understands.
characters.name: The Darkling

characters.description: A strikingly beautiful young Grisha with the rare gift of a Tailor, able to alter appearance, flesh, and beauty. She serves at the royal court and is assigned to attend Alina at the Little Palace, becoming her first real friend there. Warm and clever, Genya helps Alina navigate the unfamiliar customs and cruelties of Grisha society, though her position at court is more precarious than it appears.
characters.name: Genya

characters.description: A harsh, secretive old woman who lives apart at the Little Palace and is tasked with training Alina to control and unlock her power. Brutal in her methods and sparing with kindness, she has known the Grisha world far longer than anyone realizes. Alina resents her lessons until Baghra proves to understand the true nature of Alina's gift, and its dangers, better than anyone else.
characters.name: Baghra

characters.description: A beautiful and haughty Grisha Squaller, able to command wind and air, who trains among the elite at the Little Palace. Proud and cutting, she resents the sudden attention lavished on the untrained Alina and treats her with open contempt, becoming an early rival in the competitive world of the Second Army.
characters.name: Zoya

characters.description: A quiet, socially awkward Grisha Fabrikator, one of the makers who work steel and chemistry into remarkable devices. Far more comfortable with his craft than with people, he labors intently at the Little Palace, more interested in what he can build than in the court's politics and rivalries.
characters.name: David Kostyk

characters.description: The king's strange, unsettling spiritual adviser, a priest who moves at the edges of the royal court. Watchful and hard to read, he takes a particular interest in Alina and the religious significance others attach to the Sun Summoner, hinting at loyalties and beliefs that do not align neatly with either the crown or the Grisha.
characters.name: The Apparat

recaps.ending: Warned by Baghra, Alina learns the Darkling's real design: he is far older than he appears, he created the Shadow Fold himself with forbidden magic, and he intends to use her light to expand and command it as an instrument of conquest rather than to destroy it. She flees the Little Palace. The Darkling pursues a legendary creature, Morozova's stag, whose antlers can be made into an amplifier that would multiply Alina's power and, in his hands, let him control her. Mal, the finest tracker in the army, finds the stag. When Alina hesitates to kill it, the Darkling seizes them both, slays the stag, and fastens its antler collar around Alina's neck, binding her power to his will. He forces her onto the Shadow Fold and, to prove his mastery, uses her light to kill. Alina realizes the connection the amplifier forges links them in both directions, and she wrests control back, flooding the Fold with blinding light and breaking his hold. She and Mal, injured, escape across the Fold and flee Ravka by sea. The Darkling is not seen to die, and Alina now carries the stag's amplifier, her power exposed to the world and the Darkling still a threat as the story closes.
recaps.in_short: Alina Starkov, an unremarkable orphan and army mapmaker, discovers she is the Sun Summoner, a Grisha able to conjure light and, in legend, the only one who can destroy the Shadow Fold that divides her country of Ravka. When her power erupts to save her lifelong friend Mal during a Fold crossing, she is taken by the Darkling, leader of the Grisha, to the Little Palace to be trained. There she is dazzled by power, status, and the Darkling's attention, while an old teacher named Baghra pushes her to master her gift. Baghra finally reveals the truth: the Darkling created the Shadow Fold long ago and means to use Alina's light not to heal Ravka but to turn the Fold into a weapon of conquest. Alina flees, and the Darkling hunts a legendary stag whose antlers can be forged into an amplifier to bind and control her. Mal tracks the stag; when the Darkling catches them and forces the amplifier onto Alina, he takes her onto the Fold and kills to demonstrate his control. But the bond runs both ways, and Alina seizes command of her own power, unleashing light and escaping with Mal across the Fold to flee Ravka, with the Darkling left behind but not destroyed.

recaps.text: Alina Starkov is a slight, overlooked orphan serving as a mapmaker in Ravka's First Army, a country split in two by the Shadow Fold, a band of unnatural darkness full of winged monsters. Her one anchor is Mal, the friend she grew up with, now a celebrated tracker. When their regiment is ordered to cross the Fold, their skiff is attacked and Mal is about to be killed. In her terror Alina unleashes a blaze of light she never knew she had, driving off the creatures. The Grisha, Ravka's magic-wielders, recognize what this means: she is the Sun Summoner of legend, the one who might destroy the Fold. She is pulled away from Mal and the ordinary army and delivered to the Darkling, the ageless and powerful leader of the Grisha, who declares that she is the key to saving their nation and takes her under his command.

Alina is brought to the Little Palace, the glittering home of the Grisha elite, and thrust into a world of luxury, rivalry, and sorcery she barely understands. She befriends the kind Tailor Genya and clashes with the proud Squaller Zoya, while struggling to summon her light at will. The Darkling lavishes attention on her and speaks of the future they could build together, and Alina, long invisible, is flattered and drawn in. She is set to train under Baghra, a severe old woman whose brutal lessons finally teach her to reach her power on her own. Cut off from Mal and unsure whom to trust, Alina begins to sense that the dazzling court hides dangerous currents, and that her new life is not the rescue it first appeared to be.

Baghra reveals the truth that shatters Alina's new world: the Darkling is far older than he seems and created the Shadow Fold himself with forbidden magic, and he means to use Alina's light to turn the Fold into a weapon of conquest rather than destroy it. Warned that she is to be enslaved to his will, Alina flees the Little Palace alone into the winter, hunted. The key to his plan is a legendary creature, Morozova's stag, whose antlers can be forged into an amplifier that would vastly increase Alina's power and let the Darkling command it. As Alina runs for her life and the Darkling's forces close in, the search for the stag becomes the race that will decide whether she can escape his control or be bound to it.

Reunited with Mal, who tracks Morozova's stag, Alina finds the creature but hesitates to kill it. The Darkling seizes them both, slays the stag himself, and fastens its antler collar around Alina's neck, binding her power to his will. He takes her onto the Shadow Fold and, to demonstrate his mastery, uses her light to kill, revealing the full horror of his plan to weaponize the darkness. Alina realizes that the connection the amplifier forges runs in both directions, and she wrests control back from him, unleashing blinding light and breaking his hold. She and Mal, wounded, escape across the Fold and flee Ravka by sea. The Darkling is not seen to die, and the truth of his ambition, and of what he created, is now exposed. Alina leaves as a fugitive, carrying the stag's amplifier and the burden of a power the whole country will want to claim.

characters.description: A dhampir novice in her final year at St. Vladimir's Academy, months away from graduating as a guardian. She is bonded to Lissa Dragomir and takes on the darkness Lissa's spirit magic produces, which has left her volatile and prone to rages she cannot always explain. Since a friend was killed in front of her over the winter she has been carrying a private guilt, refusing counselling, and beginning to see things that other people do not.
characters.name: Rose Hathaway

characters.description: The last of the royal Dragomir line and Rose's bondmate, a Moroi who wields spirit and is learning to control it with Adrian Ivashkov's help rather than with medication. Her healing and compulsion are growing stronger, and so is the cost, most of which Rose absorbs without telling her. She is with Christian Ozera and being groomed by the royal families for a political future she is not sure she wants.
characters.name: Lissa Dragomir

characters.description: A Russian guardian at the Academy and Rose's combat instructor, widely regarded as one of the best fighters in Moroi society. Controlled and deliberate, he has admitted that he returns Rose's feelings and has held to the position that acting on them would compromise them both as Lissa's guardians. He is one of the few adults Rose trusts entirely.
characters.name: Dimitri Belikov

characters.description: A dhampir novice and one of Rose's closest friends, killed by a Strigoi in Spokane during the winter break while trying to protect her. Rose blames herself for his death. As the new term begins she starts glimpsing him standing silently at the edge of crowds and outside windows, watching her and never speaking.
characters.name: Mason Ashford

characters.description: A Moroi long shunned for his parents' choice to become Strigoi, sharp-tongued, defensive, and one of the only Moroi at the school willing to use his fire magic in a fight. He is Lissa's boyfriend, and his friendship with Rose is built mostly on insults.
characters.name: Christian Ozera

characters.description: A dhampir novice who survived the Spokane captivity alongside Rose and came out of it quieter and harder. He is a careful, disciplined fighter and takes the final year's assignments more seriously than anyone.
characters.name: Eddie Castile

characters.description: A royal Moroi in his twenties, the queen's great-nephew, and a spirit user who reads auras and walks into other people's dreams. He is staying near the Academy to teach Lissa how to handle spirit, and he uses dream-walking to reach Rose whenever she will not talk to him awake. He drinks and smokes heavily, partly because it dulls spirit's effects on him.
characters.name: Adrian Ivashkov

characters.description: A guardian who teaches combat theory at the Academy and has never had patience with Rose. Blunt and quick to assume the worst of her, he plays an aggressor in the novices' field assessments.
characters.name: Stan Alto

characters.description: The captain of the Academy's guardians, who designs and oversees the novices' final field experience. Fair, unsentimental and willing to hear Rose out when other staff will not.
characters.name: Alberta Petrov

characters.description: The headmistress of St. Vladimir's, rigid about procedure and still inclined to treat Rose as a discipline problem rather than a promising novice.
characters.name: Headmistress Kirova

characters.description: A Moroi prince who was arrested after kidnapping and exploiting Lissa for her healing magic, and who has spent the intervening months in custody awaiting trial. Dying of a wasting disease and utterly unrepentant, he still regards what he did as reasonable and still knows more about spirit than almost anyone alive.
characters.name: Victor Dashkov

characters.description: A non-royal Moroi girl who was once Rose and Lissa's tormentor and became an ally after her mother was killed by Strigoi. She now lives at the Royal Court, trains constantly, and has taught herself to use water magic as a weapon.
characters.name: Mia Rinaldi

characters.description: A shy Moroi underclassman, tall and awkward for her age, who idolizes Lissa and Rose from a distance. She is one of the students who takes up Christian's offer to teach Moroi to use their magic offensively.
characters.name: Jill Mastrano

recaps.ending: Warned by Mason's ghost, Rose sees Strigoi gathering outside the school's wards, and the attack comes that night. Humans working for the Strigoi have broken the wards, and the Strigoi come through in numbers no one has ever faced on Moroi ground. Students and staff are killed, and many are dragged away alive into a cave system nearby to be kept as food. A rescue party goes in after them. Rose fights through the caves alongside Christian, kills several Strigoi, and most of the captives, including Eddie, are brought out. Dimitri is not among them. When the dead are counted his body is missing, and the guardians conclude what Rose refuses to hear: he was bitten and taken alive, and has been awakened as a Strigoi. He and Rose had promised each other that neither would be left in that state, and everyone around her treats the promise as impossible to keep. Rose does not. She leaves St. Vladimir's without graduating, breaks with Lissa, who begs her to stay, and sets out for Russia, where she believes Dimitri would go, intending to find him and end it herself.
recaps.in_short: Rose returns to St. Vladimir's for her final term haunted by Mason's death and by Mason himself, whose silent ghost keeps appearing to her. She is assigned to guard Christian Ozera for the novices' six-week field experience rather than Lissa, and her visions cost her badly when she freezes during a staged attack and is hauled before a disciplinary hearing. At the Royal Court, Victor Dashkov is convicted and imprisoned for what he did to Lissa. Rose learns that being shadow-kissed, brought back from the dead, is why the dead can reach her, and that Mason has been trying to warn her rather than accuse her. She and Dimitri finally give in to what they feel and spend a night together, and he says he will step aside as her instructor so they can be together openly. Hours later the Strigoi come. The wards have been broken by human accomplices, the school is overrun, and the survivors are taken into nearby caves. Rose fights in the rescue, but Dimitri is taken alive and turned Strigoi. Rose leaves school and the country to hunt him down and keep the promise they made each other.

recaps.text: Previously: Rose Hathaway is a dhampir novice at St. Vladimir's Academy, training to guard the living Moroi vampires against the undead Strigoi. She is bonded to her best friend Lissa Dragomir, the last of a royal line, because Lissa unknowingly used spirit magic to bring Rose back from death as a child; Rose can feel Lissa's emotions, enter her mind, and absorb the madness spirit leaves behind, and is called shadow-kissed for it. Lissa was tormented and finally kidnapped by Victor Dashkov, a family friend who wanted her healing for his own fatal illness; he was caught and awaits trial. Rose trains under the guardian Dimitri Belikov, and the two are in love and forbidden to act on it. Over the winter, coordinated Strigoi attacks with human helpers forced the school to move the holiday to a guarded ski resort. There Rose met Adrian Ivashkov, an idle royal Moroi who is also a spirit user, and learned that Christian's aunt Tasha had asked Dimitri to leave the Academy for her. Rose repeated a rumour about a Strigoi nest in Spokane, and her friend Mason went after it. All of them were captured, and Mason was killed in front of Rose before she destroyed the two Strigoi. Dimitri refused Tasha and stayed. Rose came back marked as a Strigoi killer, silently grieving, and seeing Mason's ghost.

The final term opens with the novices' field experience: for six weeks each novice is assigned a Moroi to guard around the clock while guardians stage surprise attacks to test them. Rose expects Lissa and is given Christian Ozera instead, because the bond would tell her where Lissa is and make the test meaningless; Eddie draws Lissa. Rose takes the assignment as an insult and Christian enjoys it. Underneath the routine, Rose is in worse shape than anyone knows. She refuses to talk about Mason's death, she is carrying more of Lissa's spirit darkness than ever, and she has begun seeing Mason himself, standing silent and unmoving at the edges of crowds. She tells no one, on the reasonable assumption that they will conclude she has lost her mind.

During a staged attack, Stan Alto grabs Christian while Rose stands frozen, staring at Mason's ghost, and does nothing. Stan reports it as deliberate, and Rose is put in front of a hearing where she cannot explain herself without admitting to hallucinations. Dimitri argues for her, but the damage to her record is real and she is punished. Her temper is worse, her mood swings sharper, and she begins to suspect the darkness she draws off Lissa is doing more to her than she has admitted. Lissa, meanwhile, is being drawn deeper into royal politics and is quietly using compulsion in situations that do not require it, which unsettles Rose more than the ghosts do.

Rose, Lissa, Christian and Dimitri travel to the Royal Court for Victor Dashkov's trial, and Rose is required to testify about the kidnapping and about the charm Victor used on her and Dimitri. Victor, visibly dying, defends himself as a man who did what the situation required and warns Lissa that she will end up understanding him. He is convicted and sentenced to prison. At Court, Rose sees Mia Rinaldi, now living there and training seriously, and spends time with Adrian, who reads her aura and tells her something in it has changed since Spokane. The ghosts follow Rose the whole trip, which finally convinces her they are not simply a symptom of grief.

Back at school, Rose stops hiding the visions from everyone and starts working out what they mean. She learns that being brought back from death has left her standing partly on the other side of it: the dead are drawn to her, and outside the school's wards they can reach her freely. There is precedent in the history of St. Vladimir, a spirit-using saint whose own shadow-kissed guardian was said to have gone mad. Mason is not accusing her. He is trying to tell her something, and Rose begins to follow him instead of turning away. The strain of taking Lissa's darkness keeps rising, and the field experience grinds on with Christian, who has started teaching younger Moroi to use their magic offensively.

Rose and Dimitri stop pretending. After the field experience ends and Rose reaches the end of what she can hold in, the two of them spend a night together in a cabin at the edge of the campus and say plainly that they are in love. Dimitri decides he will resign as her instructor and ask to be reassigned so that they can be together without either of them being compromised, and for the first time Rose can see a future that contains both her duty and him. That same day Mason's ghost appears again, more insistent than before, and leads Rose to look beyond the wards, where she sees Strigoi assembled in numbers no one has ever reported and realizes the school is about to be attacked.

Rose raises the alarm and, after some resistance, is believed. It is already too late. The wards have been sabotaged by humans working for the Strigoi, and the attackers come through the campus at night in a coordinated assault, killing students, staff and guardians. Rather than feeding on the spot, many Strigoi drag captives away alive into a cave system beyond the school grounds, to keep as a food supply until they can be turned or killed. The surviving guardians assemble a rescue party, and Rose insists on going in with it. The fighting in the caves is close, dark and brutal, and Rose kills more Strigoi than she can keep count of, with Christian burning a path beside her.

Most of the captives are brought out alive, Eddie among them, and the Strigoi in the caves are destroyed. When the losses are counted, Dimitri is not on either list. His body is not found, and a guardian confirms what Rose saw in the caves: he was bitten and taken alive, which means he has been awakened as a Strigoi. Every adult treats him as dead and unreachable. Rose remembers what she and Dimitri promised each other, that neither would leave the other to exist that way, and decides she is the only person who will keep it. She turns down the chance to graduate, tells Lissa she is going and breaks their bond of trust in the process, and leaves the country for Russia, where she believes he would have gone, carrying a stake and no plan beyond finding him.
